title: Investigating the Potential of CDDO-Me as an HMGB1 Inhibitor in Mitigating Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
authors: Zhang, Libang; Li, Guolong; Chen, Xingru; Li, Tian; Raj, Richa; Shen, Pingping
journal: Journal of neuroimmune pharmacology : the official journal of the Society on NeuroImmune Pharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CDDO-Me与HMGB1蛋白结合抑制神经炎症，虽含MD模拟但对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: HMGB1-mediated neuroinflammation assumes a pivotal position in the pathophysiological framework of a multitude of neurological disorders, including ischemic stroke, which still urgently need effective therapeutic agents. CDDO-Me, is a potentially useful therapeutic drug for diabetic nephropathy, whereas the neuroprotective properties and underlying mechanism in ischemic stroke have not been reported as yet. In the present study, CDDO-Me was found to alleviate OGD/R induced nerve cell injury and protect the cerebral ischemia of rats. In addition, the proinflammatory activity of HMGB1 was inhibited by CDDO-Me through directly binding to HMGB1 and then disrupting its interaction with receptor TLR4. The binding affinity of CDDO-Me to HMGB1 was 117 microM indicated by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay. On this basis, we observed that CDDO-Me could slightly change the secondary and steric conformation as well as the thermal stability of HMGB1. Subsequently, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation showed that CDDO-Me mainly binds to the A-box domain of HMGB1, which was maintained by weak interaction forces like van der Waals and hydrophobicity. Further virtual mutagenesis and binding free energy calculations identified F38 and F89 in the A-box as key residues involved in HMGB1-CDDO-Me interaction. These findings indicated that CDDO-Me can improve stroke-induced inflammatory damage through direct binding HMGB1 and negative regulation of HMGB1-TLR4 downstream cytokine signaling activity.
abstract_zh: HMGB1介导的神经炎症在多种神经系统疾病的病理生理框架中占据关键地位，包括缺血性卒中，而这类疾病仍迫切需要有效的治疗药物。CDDO-Me是糖尿病肾病的一种潜在有用治疗药物，但其在缺血性卒中中的神经保护特性及潜在机制尚未见报道。在本研究中，发现CDDO-Me能减轻OGD/R诱导的神经细胞损伤，并保护大鼠脑缺血。此外，CDDO-Me通过直接结合HMGB1并破坏其与受体TLR4的相互作用，抑制了HMGB1的促炎活性。表面等离子体共振（SPR）实验显示，CDDO-Me与HMGB1的结合亲和力为117微摩尔。在此基础上，我们观察到CDDO-Me能轻微改变HMGB1的二级结构和空间构象以及热稳定性。随后，分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟显示，CDDO-Me主要结合于HMGB1的A-box结构域，该结合由范德华力和疏水作用等弱相互作用力维持。进一步的虚拟突变和结合自由能计算确定了A-box中的F38和F89为参与HMGB1-CDDO-Me相互作用的关键残基。这些发现表明，CDDO-Me可通过直接结合HMGB1并负调控HMGB1-TLR4下游细胞因子信号活性，改善卒中诱导的炎症损伤。
